    Layers
    Why two lines?

    Sky lines choose how the bright line is drawn. In space is the true orbit: one ellipse fixed in space, each lap lying exactly on the last. Seen from Earth is the path an observer on the ground sees, which is what a pass looks like from here: the Earth keeps turning, so it never repeats.

    Ground track (thin, on the Earth): the Earth turns under that ellipse, 15° an hour, so one lap (~93 min for the ISS) later the satellite passes about 23° further west. Laps never overlap and the lines look as if they cross, yet nothing ever crosses its own orbit. The two lines show different moments: the dots tell how many minutes ahead each point is.
